title: Find Two Products Within a Budget
real_world_story: A customer has a fixed shopping budget and wants to purchase exactly two products. Find whether there are two products whose combined price is exactly equal to the customer's budget.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Efficiently finding a pair of products that matches the target budget

problem_statement: Given an array of product prices and a target budget B, determine whether there are two different products whose prices add up exactly to B.
task: Return the indices of the two products whose combined price equals the target budget. If no such pair exists, return -1 -1.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N integers representing product prices. The third line contains an integer B representing the target budget.
output_format: Print two indices representing a valid product pair. If multiple solutions exist, any valid pair may be returned. If no pair exists, print -1 -1.

examples.explanation: The products at indices 0 and 1 cost 300 and 700, which total 1000, so this example would not be valid for a target of 1500.

expected_algorithm.name: Two Pointer
expected_algorithm.reason: After sorting the prices, one pointer can start at the lowest price and another at the highest price. The pointers can move toward each other depending on the current sum.

hint: First think about ordering the product prices.
Place one pointer at the beginning and another at the end.
If the current sum is too small, move the left pointer.
If the current sum is too large, move the right pointer.
real_world_takeaway: The two-pointer technique can turn a potentially expensive pair-search into an efficient solution after sorting the data.
